newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania races against time to complete sowing.
newsitem.headline: Romania races against time to complete sowing.

text.p: Romania hopes to complete maize sowing on a planned 3.1 million hectares this week in a race against time to recoup delays in seasonal work caused by adverse weather last month, officials said on Monday.
"We will complete maize sowing at the weekend," agriculture ministry director Matei Georgescu told Reuters.
Heavy rains and low temperatures last month delayed the sowing of maize, sugar beet, sunflower and fodder plants.
A ministry official said some 1.72 million ha, or some 55 percent of the planned area, had been put under maize so far.
Quoting data gathered by the ministry last Friday, the official said sugar beet had been sown on 117,063 ha, or 84 percent of the planned 138,401 ha.
Sunflower had been sown on 547,239 ha, or 69 percent of the planned 781,822 ha, he said.
"We are racing against time. It's very important to maintain the present pace of works. One should also pray for good weather," the official said.
Reports in the local media in recent weeks said delays in completing seasonal work could jeopardise grain crops, especially as high humidity in the plains had favoured a strong growth of weeds.
But Georgescu said farmers had already spread herbicides on large areas and that there was "no danger to the crops, including wheat".
Ministry data showed 989,840 ha of the 2.3 million ha put under wheat had been treated with herbicides as of last Friday.
"I don't rule out some minor losses, especially in the hilly areas, but they won't be significant. We count on a good crop of wheat," Georgescu said.

Last week, Agriculture Minister Dinu Gavrilescu forecast a bumper wheat crop and exports amounting to some 1.5 million tonnes this year, which could bring Romania back among the major players on the world grain market.
Gavrilescu said he expected this year's wheat crop to amount to the level recorded in 1995, when Romania harvested 7.8 million tonnes and sold over 1.3 million.

Last year, Romania had 2.11 million hectares sown to wheat, but an early winter and late snow damaged the crop on almost half that area. The country harvested just 3.1 million tonnes in 1996, a record low.
